description: This course makes an initial approach to the vast archive of 20th and 21st century African-American literature. Studying a broad range of literary genres and forms, students focus on the radical ways Black writers have wielded language to address the living history of enslavement, or what Saidiya Hartman has called the "afterlife of slavery." Students explore how African-American writers interrogate race as a form of knowledge and experience and, at the same time, often address related questions of gender, sexuality, and class.
